To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the generic weak-ming angle relation sin2(theta_W)~ N/(N+2) can be satisfied with N=5 colors and M_U ~ 1016 GeV if light Higgs doublet are added to the standard model.
the grand unification of the gauge couplings is achieved in the presence of a single light Higgs doublet when the color group is SU(N) with N=5 or N=7 at the GUT unification scale.

(1) The weak mixing angle is a function of the number of generations of quarks and leptons, N, at the grand unification scale, M_{GUT}. (2) The value of the weak mixing angle, as determined by the LEP experiments, requires N=7 at M_{GUT} = 10^{17} GeV, and N=5 at the scale M_{GUT}\simeq 10^{16} GeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects that an external magnetic field has on the dynamics of a system of interacting particles.
the study of the properties of the quark-antiquark potential in QCD, and the application of this potential in the description of hadrons.
the study of the effects of the Higgs boson mass on the electroweak phase transition in the Standard Model and in extensions with a singlet field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the standard model of elementary particle physics, as it is known today, is not the final theory of the fundamental forces.
there is no evidence for any kind of new physics in this region of mass and energy.
, while the standard model is an excellent description of all available experimental data, it is a theory of physics which is incomplete and, in fact, is not self-consistent at the fundamental level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gauge coupling constant unification is a very robust phenomenon, and it can occur with a wide range of particle content.
the gauge coupling unification can be achieved by increasing the number of colors at higher energies.

we have found the first example of a grand unification with a large number of colors and light Higgs doublet(s) that satisfies all low-energy constraints, and that it may be possible to achieve such a unification at a scale M_U ~10^17 Gev.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a gauge coupling grand unified theory with the standard model particle spectrum can be realized in the minimal standard model framework if the number of QCD degrees of freedoms increases with increasing energy.
the standard model with a single Higgs doublet is a special case, not a general case, in grand unification.
the weak mixing angle relation is a powerful tool for constraining the particle content of a grand unified theory.
